title: Lattice gauge theory as a proposed $q\to 1$ shadow of the $q$-deformed surface state-sum
html:
Remark. Lattice gauge theory as a proposed q\to 1 shadow of the q-deformed surface state-sum

The non-abelian Stokes representation of the archimedean functor writes each observable's holonomy as a surface-ordered integral of the q-deformed curvature F_q over a spanning Seifert surface \Sigma,

  \mathrm{Hol}(\partial\Sigma) \;=\; \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathcal{P}}\!\!\int_{\Sigma} F_q .

Discretizing \Sigma — tessellating it into cells that each carry quantum-group data, with the surface-ordered product in the role of the 2-holonomy — realizes a q-deformed lattice gauge theory on the surface.

Two features separate it from a naive lattice regularization. First, the q-deformed surface state-sum is triangulation-invariant: refining the tessellation leaves the holonomy unchanged, so no continuum limit in the cell size is required and no per-cell coupling is free to tune. Second, the deformation carries an intrinsic geometric scale hierarchy q^{-n}, so a nested tessellation supplies its own regulator; the cell size is a computational scaffold rather than a physical scale.

Ordinary lattice quantum chromodynamics is recovered as the q\to 1 (classical) shadow of this construction: the quantum-group cell data degenerate to ordinary gauge holonomies and the surface-ordered product becomes the plaquette product of the Wilson action.

This correspondence is a structural observation, not a theorem. Agreement between a q-deformed surface state-sum and a lattice-gauge computation is an empirical cross-check — of the same evidential tier as agreement with an experimental datum, and strictly weaker than a formal derivation. A proof of the state-sum / lattice-gauge correspondence remains open.
